title: Performance panel overview
learningObjectives: Explain performance panel overview and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: The Performance panel records runtime activity such as scripting, style recalculation, layout, paint, rendering, and long tasks. It provides a timeline for identifying where the main thread spends time during an interaction.
understand.whyItMatters: Profiling helps target actual bottlenecks. Avoid optimising based only on intuition or one synthetic measurement.
understand.analogy: A performance recording is a timeline that shows where time was spent during a journey.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The User Timing API marks and measures a small operation; the Performance panel provides broader rendering and scripting detail.

examples.explanation: The User Timing API marks and measures a small operation; the Performance panel provides broader rendering and scripting detail.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the workflow or developer-tool concept; command examples require a practice repository.

practise.guidedTask: Record a slow interaction and identify scripting, layout, paint, and long-task sections. Compare after one targeted change.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.
